column2: CPU hold limit: the CPU never holds the ball longer than ai_hold_limit (new setting, 2.5 s; people have no limit). From 0.32 s before it, whatever it was doing, it dunks if a dunk is ready, lets a cocked shot go if that is legal, or else passes (charged past the dribble threshold, so the seated rule and the dribble cap cannot stop it; with the shot cocked the jump stays down so the bounce goes first); every level's patience is capped at the limit minus 0.7 s. Overheating rim: a player staying on or in a rim (any body part within the rim opening +14 px, 50 px above to 60 px below it, both feet clear of the floor) heats it over rim_heat_time (2 s; cools over rim_cool_time 1 s when left), the rim glows red to hot orange to a crimson-white core with a pulsing glow and rising sparks, then a white gleam sweeps along it and back (rim_gleam_time 0.45 s) and it blows: fire burst, boom, shake, a small OVERHEAT! at the rim, any hang let go, and everyone on it sent down at rim_blast (6 px/step, gentle); ordinary hanging dunks (0.9 s) never get that hot. Hand on the floor, a hard rule: every step a hand touches the floor, unless the body is already turning away, the wobble is turned the other way (no cooldown, no 'still turning toward it' condition, a small lift when lying flat; hand_push 0.08 -> 0.1). Legend and Mythic take good-but-not-perfect shots; the Mythic still waits for a perfect line when one exists, and takes a good one when none is left in the cock-back (no more dribbling out of dead shots).

column2: Bug fixes. No lining up: the Mythic's wait for a perfect line is gone (text 'LINING UP A PERFECT SHOT' and the LINING UP brief removed); every level takes the first line that is on, and from level 4 a line the cock-back has already carried well past its spot (two steps running) is not let go but pumped out of while a dribble is allowed (a line that jumps the window inside one step is let go). Rim blast much larger: everything within rim_blast_radius (new, 300 px) of the rim is thrown outward, hardest at the centre (rim_blast 6 -> 16 px/step), players as whole bodies, the ball too (out of any hand, its shot cleared); a 3x fire burst, smoke, sparks, a shockwave ring out to the radius, a white flash, a bigger shake and a bigger OVERHEAT! call. Own goals: fadeaways only with ai_fade_room (new, 260 px) between the carrier and the rim it defends (fades drift back: that is how a fade then the outlet pass from the air ended in its own basket); a cocked shot under its own rim passes nothing from the air (the jump stays down until the feet are down, then the outlet); from behind its own rim the outlet is a floor pass, never a self-pass; and, as a last resort, holding the ball over its own rim's opening with the feet off the floor (a ball taken off a dunk or rebound at the rim mouth: the rim counts as ground, which is why sinceGround missed it) it clears it with an instant shot. Ball as an extension of the hand: a carrier's (or dunker's) ball touching the floor triggers the same hand-on-floor reversal. Moves. Alley-oop lob: let go only when Physics.lobReceiver is set and the flight is at least as long as his planned jump; if that never comes in 0.9 s it becomes a jump shot (or a pump); a defender within ai_lob_guard (new, 150 px) of the board stops it at every lob level (the Mythic used to lob regardless); its own lob record (mine.lob) moves its taste for it. Screen (level 4+): the one key hops both men, so it screens only when the dribbler is already up or the ball is rising into his hand and he leans toward it. Pump fake: never into a defender's hand right in front (level 4+); the follow-up waits for the baited defender to land (or 0.25 s if he never went up, at most 0.5 s); a pump counts against the dribble budget; a Legend or Mythic fakes less when its fakes keep failing to reach a shot. Fadeaway: only against a defender in front, with room behind; level 5+ waits at most 0.6 s for the lean, then goes straight up. Self-pass: thrown is marked when the pass leaves (an immediate re-catch now counts); the outlet self-pass is thrown short (lowest charge 0.35-0.5 that clears the rim zone) and only with nobody within 120 px. Fast break: the Legend leads the runner too and the throw is sized to where he will be. Outlet and wall pass: the quickest pass with a defender within 90 px, otherwise the charge (0.3-0.7) whose flown-out landing is most open (Physics.pathFrom, new). Long shot for 2: from level 4 no urgency bonus for a shot with no line on target; Legend/Mythic +0.15 for an open long shot. Defence: dunk swat timed (level 5+) to the slam from the dunk's plan; early rim read for the Legend (rimLead 6); timed steal (level 5+) times the raised hand of a held jump to the ball path and skips a ball its dribbler takes back first; swipe (level 5+) only at a ball within arm's reach and not shielded behind the carrier; board crash (level 5+) sends the man on the floor; a rim protector is waited out at most 0.8/1.0/1.6 s (levels 4/5/6), and from level 5 an open pass, lob or shot over him is taken instead. A/B at level 4 showed the swipe reach test cost it (50-91 with it, 72-66 without) while helping levels 5-6, so it applies from level 5; a new board-crash spot for the miss's direction did worse and was dropped. New tools/ai-moves.js: the per-move probe.

column2: CPU dribble cap: one CPU dribble carries the ball and the dribbler (the feet: the swing tilts the torso over them) at most ai_dribble_reach (new, 20 px) toward the rim it attacks; physics w.dribCap per team, set for the CPU's teams; past it every forward speed is taken away, checked one step ahead and again after any hop. Alley-oop: the receiver may stand up to lob_reach (new, 340 px; was a fixed 260) from the rim (a trace found the receiver out of reach in 3 of 4 chances; thrown lobs already ended in dunks 4 times in 6). Give-and-go (new): a forward pass caught, its passer (within about 420 px of the dunk spot, the receiver far enough out) cuts for the rim in quick low hops (cut_rise 40, cut_vx_max 13, kept upright); a pass straight back to him within give_go_window (2.2 s) is an alley-oop catch, and caught in reach it goes up for the dunk by itself; callout GIVE-AND-GO! and score name. The CPU sets it up from the front court (PASS AND CUT), waits for the cutter, and throws to where he will be once he will be in dunk reach. Putback (new): a miss caught in the air within putback_window (1.5 s) of the shot is dunked straight back if the rim is in reach (no press needed); callout PUTBACK!; the CPU's spare man crashes the board for its own misses from level 3. Heat check (new): the same player scoring heat_streak (3) times in a row is hot until the other team scores: flame trail, HEAT CHECK! call, shots helped by heat_assist (0.85) instead of shot_assist; the CPU feeds a hot teammate, shoots more when hot and guards a hot carrier closer. column2: CPU defence against long shots, and decisions for levels 3-5 (AI only, no rule change). It reads the long-shot threat: the lines the carrier has from where he stands (the same shot preview, run on him: perfect, on target, none) and a scouting record of his long shots by 100 px distance band (made, perfect), trusted by how much it has seen and how much the level learns. It closes out: the target becomes a spot a hand's reach in front of the shooter, led by his drift (L3 only on a perfect line once he cocks; L4 on any line on target; L5-6 also on a spot the scouting says he hits from), sprinting in longer hops; a closeout can overcommit past him (the level's slip), which a fake or a drive beats. From level 4 it contests a long shot's path: the ball's early flight from the predicted release (shotVelocity + pathFrom) against the closer's raised hand over a held jump; it jumps when they meet. Decisions (3+): a shot's worth blends its own record of that kind open or pressed over the prior; levels 3-5 hold a choice longer (14/10/6 steps), and a Pro with two near-equal options hesitates a moment (THINKING IT OVER); an open long shot is taken from level 3 (OPEN: TAKING THE TWO); a pump fake also answers a closer flying at it. The I panel shows the scouting line. New tools/ai-longd.js.

column2: CPU rule: no dunk off the dribble. A CPU player who has dribbled may not dunk until the ball leaves him (a pass, a self-pass, a shot, or another player taking it); his teammate may dunk his pass, and he may dunk after catching his own self-pass. Physics: w.noDunkAfterDribble per team (set for the CPU's teams; setting ai_no_dribble_dunk, 1 = on); p.dribbled set on his dribble, cleared on his pass or shot or any other player's catch; while it is set the dunk prompt stays off (a press cocks a shot) and startDunk refuses. AI: a carrier who has dribbled no longer waits at the rim for a dunk or drives at it for one (the dribble is worth less the nearer the rim), and near the rim it shoots, passes, lobs or self-passes; intent NO DUNK OFF THE DRIBBLE.
